title: Producer contract
description:
A CAPABILITY CLAIM, never a completion claim (ADR-0602). The autogenesis operation registry (`artifacts/autogenesis/operations.json`) is a retrospective RECEIPT: every admission arm requires `epistemic_status: "proved"`, so it cannot express 'we could attempt this open fact' without asserting a proof that does not exist. A producer contract fills that gap with a different, narrower claim: facts matching this SHAPE are dischargeable via route R using recipe X. It says nothing about whether any particular match has been attempted or has succeeded.

FALSIFIABILITY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT PROSE. There is no `proved` field, no `epistemic_status` field, and no field of that shape anywhere in this schema -- `additionalProperties: false` at every level makes smuggling one in a schema violation, not a reviewable choice. A contract cannot assert completed work because completed work has nowhere to be written.

THE VACUOUS-MATCHER DEFECT IS THE ONE THIS SCHEMA EXISTS TO PREVENT. A shape predicate that matches every open fact is not a capability claim, it is a blank check, and `scripts/validate-producer-contracts.py` rejects any contract whose predicate matches every open fact in the ledger. `non_examples` is the falsifiability requirement made structural: at least one fact id the predicate is claimed NOT to match, checked by EXECUTING the predicate against the real fact (never by trusting the claim).

id.description: Stable identifier. Versioned (`-vN`) because a shape predicate is expected to be refined as the pool of open facts it claims to cover changes.

route.description: The ADR-0601 SS4 producer route that would discharge a match: `kernel-lane` (a proving lane constructs a kernel term), `cas-bridge` (the CAS-to-kernel bridge reconstructs a CAS certificate), or `import` (the ADR-0601 SS3 backlog artifact). `kernel-lane` capability always exists; `cas-bridge` and `import` are capable only once their own artifact exists -- `fact-frontier.py` checks this, absent-tolerantly, since both are sibling deliverables under construction.

description.description: What a lane or tool actually DOES with a match: which generic checker, proposer, or bridge stage receives it. Prose, reviewed like any other claim -- never itself evidence that the recipe was run.

reference.description: Optional repository-relative path to the generic producer/checker code this recipe dispatches to (e.g. a `crates/axeyum-lean-import/examples/*.rs` shape-generic checker). Documentation only; not verified to exist by the validator, since a recipe may name work still in flight on a sibling lane.

shape.description: The executable predicate. Every field is a positive constraint (ANDed together): a fact must satisfy every field present to match. At least one of `title_prefix`, `statement_contains`, or `id_prefix` is REQUIRED by the validator (not expressible in JSON Schema alone) -- `formal_language`/`fragments` alone is too coarse a shape and risks becoming the vacuous matcher this schema exists to forbid.

formal_language.description: A fact matches only if `formal.language` is one of these.

fragments.description: A fact matches only if `formal.fragment` is one of these.

title_prefix.description: A fact matches only if `title` starts with this string.

statement_contains.description: A fact matches only if `formal.statement` contains this substring.

id_prefix.description: A fact matches only if `id` starts with this string.

non_examples.description: At least one real fact id the shape predicate provably does NOT match -- the falsifiability requirement (ADR-0602). Checked by EXECUTING `shape` against the named fact's current ledger entry, never by trusting `reason`.

reason.description: Which constraint the fact fails and why -- reviewed prose, not itself checked; the executable check is the predicate re-run against the fact.
